exploration.title: Sound Playground
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.summary: Predict and compare how string length and modeled displacement change frequency and wave height.
exploration.question: How can two plucks keep the same modeled frequency while their vibration heights differ?
exploration.explanation: Frequency counts cycles per second and strongly influences perceived pitch, but frequency and pitch are not identical. For this ideal uniform string’s fixed-end fundamental, doubling length while holding tension and mass per length fixed halves frequency. Doubling the modeled displacement does not change that natural frequency; it quadruples an A² comparison index. That index is not a decibel or loudness reading. Real musical sounds also depend on harmonics, the instrument body and how the sound changes over time.

experiments.title: Compare string lengths
experiments.instruction: Keep tension and model displacement fixed. Predict what happens when vibrating length doubles from 60 to 120 cm, then run the fixed comparison.
experiments.observe: The longer trial has half as many cycles per second. Use the unchanged-variable list to explain why length caused the difference.

experiments.title: Compare model displacements
experiments.instruction: Keep length and tension fixed. Predict whether changing modeled displacement from 3 to 6 mm changes frequency, then run the fixed comparison.
experiments.observe: Frequency stays the same while wave height and the relative A² index change. Explain why this is not a loudness measurement.

exploration.misconception: A taller modeled wave is not automatically a higher pitch or a direct loudness reading. Frequency strongly influences pitch; perceived loudness depends on sound level, frequency, hearing and listening conditions.
